name: NY-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with an 11-point partisan lean
Incumbent Tim Kennedy running with a large fundraising edge ($2.3M raised, $1.2M on hand)
Prediction markets price Kennedy near 97% to win
No public polling or expert ratings, so uncertainty rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Kennedy: an 11-point Democratic lean, incumbency, a favorable environment, and a dominant fundraising position against a little-known challenger with no reported money. Markets agree, pricing Kennedy at roughly 97%, so the forecast stays near the baseline with only a small discount for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Kennedy underperforming his district lean, or a surge of outside spending for Hannon, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Western New York's 26th District leans Democratic by about 11 points, and first-term incumbent Tim Kennedy is running for reelection with a substantial financial advantage. He has raised roughly $2.3 million and holds about $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Dennis Hannon reports no fundraising figures in the record. No outside spending has been reported on either side.

With no public polls and no expert ratings, the race is judged on fundamentals, which point firmly to Kennedy. Prediction markets price his chances near 97 percent. The forecast places the expected margin in the low twenties for Kennedy, with moderate uncertainty given the lack of direct polling in the district.
